newsitem.title: MEXICO: Companies bid for Mexico's Merida III power plant.
newsitem.headline: Companies bid for Mexico's Merida III power plant.

text.p: Six business groups from the United States, Japan, Holland and Canada along with domestic companies have presented proposals to construct a thermoelectric energy plant Merida III in Mexico's Yucatan state, the Federal Electricity Commission said Tuesday.
The domestic firms included Empresas ICA Sociedad Controladora, Grupo Tribasa and Gutsa Construcciones.
Foreign companies included Mitsubishi Electric Corp., General Electric Co., Nichimen Corp., Marubeni Corp., Destec Energy Inc. and Itochu Corp., the commission said.
Construction plans for the Merida III plant have been delayed at least three years. The 450 megawatt site is seen as setting the tone for the government's future energy generation investment plans.
A total of 18 domestic and foreign companies compose the consortia interested in constructing and operating the project, expected to require an investment of $450 million, the commission said.

"This is the first contest for independent energy production taking place in Mexico as part of the national electricity expansion program, which aims to establish projects in the next five years of 9,000 megawatts," the commission said in a statement.
On Jan. 16 the government will accept bids to build a gas pipeline connecting the states of Tabasco and Yucatan to provide fuel for the Merida III plant.

A week later Mexico will assess the technical offers and unseal the economic offers for the plant, with a decision on the winner expected Feb. 23. Construction is expected to begin in 1997 with operations beginning in 2000, the commission said.
